title: Point sections and constant-sheaf reconstruction
statement: Fix $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$ in the point setting [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Put $(R,B)=(A_{E,n},(A_{E,n})_s)$ or $(\mathcal O_E,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s})$. For an $R$-module $M$ let $\underline M$ be its constant sheaf on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and put $L_R(M)=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$, using the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Apply $L_R$ and $\Gamma(s,-)$ termwise to complexes. Assume these functors are exact and $\Gamma(s,B)=R$ through the constant-value map. Use their explicit adjunction, sending $h:L_RM\to F$ to $(m\mapsto h_s(1\otimes m))$, with inverse $t\mapsto(b\otimes m\mapsto b\,t(m)|_U)$ over each object $U$. For every bounded finite-cohomology complex $c$ over $A_{E,n}$, or bounded finitely generated-cohomology complex $c$ over $\mathcal O_E$, its adjunction unit $c\to\Gamma(s,L_Rc)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $L_Rc$ belongs to $D^b_c(s,R)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. In the integral case $c$ has a bounded finite-projective representative $P$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], and $L_RP$ is a constructible representative of $L_Rc$. For every $C\in D^b_c(s,R)$ with $c=\Gamma(s,C)$, the actual adjunction counit $L_Rc\to C$ is an isomorphism. These units and counits are natural in $c$ and $C$.

proof.text: Use the given exact adjunction and its canonical termwise derived adjunction. Evaluation at 1 identifies maps from the coefficient regular module and maps from the unit sheaf with the same final-object sections, so the left adjoint sends the regular module to the unit sheaf. The scalar-section bijection makes the unit invertible on the regular module. Finite products and cokernels extend this to every finitely presented module. Exact homology comparison and the localization formulas for the actual adjunction unit and counit upgrade cohomology isomorphisms to derived isomorphisms.

source.place: Second sentence: extension/sections identification; exact localization expanded by the agent.

proof.text: At finite level the quotient coefficient ring is finite. A finite module is finitely presented by Mathlib, so step 1 proves its unit invertible. The constant-module encoding identifies the left adjoint with ordinary constant sheafification by uniqueness of left adjoints. The constant module is finite locally constant on the etale point. Comparison preserves constructibility and constant sheaves, and the encoding transports this to intrinsic pro-etale module constructibility.

source.place: Finite-stage reconstruction: finite presentations and the single-stratum constructibility definition.

proof.text: Finite-ring constructible origin writes each finite constructible pro-etale module as the comparison pullback of an etale constructible module. Forgetting module structure, the algebraically closed-point theorem makes the etale constant-sheaf counit invertible; compatibility with forgetting reflects this for modules. Finiteness of the constant etale module sheaf makes its value finitely generated, hence finite over the finite coefficient ring. Thus the original module is isomorphic to the constant realization of a finite module. The adjunction triangle identity and the invertible unit show that its actual counit is invertible.

source.place: Tags 09AK (lemma-compare-constructible), 099Y (lemma-compare-locally-constant); algebraically closed-point description as recorded in the cited node.

proof.text: Apply exact homology comparison to the finite-cohomology complex: the same finite support is preserved and step 2 gives constructibility in every degree. Step 1 gives the derived unit. For a constructible finite complex, step 3 makes every cohomology counit invertible, hence the derived counit is invertible. Also finite constructible modules with zero sections vanish: each is constant and the adjunction triangle identity makes it a retract of the constant object on its sections. Applying this degreewise shows finite constructible complexes with zero derived sections vanish.

source.place: Derived finite-stage reconstruction; cohomology upgrade of the previous two steps.

proof.text: The valuation ring is a PID domain. For each finite module choose a finite free surjection using Mathlib. Its kernel is finitely generated over the Noetherian PID and free as a submodule of a free module. The short exact sequence therefore gives a two-term finite-projective resolution. The single-object short exact triangle, perfect triangle closure and bounded perfect-cohomology assembly produce a bounded finite-projective representative of each complex with bounded finitely generated cohomology. Finite modules over the PID are finitely presented, so step 1 also proves the integral derived unit.

source.place: Tags 0AUW (lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat), 066U (lemma-cohomology-perfect); finite free resolutions: algebra.tex Tag 00LP.

proof.text: The completed regular coefficient sheaf in degree zero is integral constructible. Step 1 identifies it with extension of the regular coefficient module. Pull integral constructibility back along the exact derived extension functor. This object property is triangulated and isomorphism-closed. Finite products put all finite free modules in it. The PID presentations of step 5 and their short exact triangles put every finite module in degree zero in it. Bounded truncation devissage then puts every bounded finite-cohomology complex in it. Transport along the perfect representative isomorphism yields the final constructible representative clause.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11; Proposition 6.8.11(3); single-stratum perfect model and the explicit uniform-bound clause in the cited characterization.

proof.text: Sections finiteness puts sections of an integral constructible object in the bounded finitely generated module class. Compare the small and standard module localizations through a common cochain representative and their homology-factorization isomorphisms. Steps 5 and 6 give the invertible unit and constructibility of its extended sections. The right triangle identity makes sections of the actual counit invertible. Triangulated integral constructibility contains its cone Z. Exact sections kill Z. The sections/reduction comparison and exactness of derived quotient tensor imply that every finite reduction of Z has zero sections. Step 4 kills those reductions. Their restrictions are zero; their product is zero by the product universal property. The canonical completeness Roos triangle of Z has two zero vertices, hence Z is zero. The counit cone criterion proves the counit invertible.

source.place: Integral counit: triangle identity, sections/reduction comparison, finite reconstruction, and the completeness triangle.

proof.text: The maps throughout are the given adjunction unit and counit and the canonical localized adjunction unit and counit. Their naturality and triangle equations are part of these natural transformations, so no representative choices change the resulting morphisms.

source.place: Naturality of the displayed unit and counit formulas.

Steps: (1) the explicit adjunction descends because both functors are exact, which the item assumes. (2) A_{E,n} is finite, a finite presentation gives the unit, and L_R M is constant with stalks M, hence constructible. (3) Finite-ring constructible origin, constancy on the algebraically closed point, and the finite comparison unit show the evaluation counit is an isomorphism; the triangle-identity check agrees. (4) The cohomology criterion gives the derived finite stage, so a constructible complex with zero sections is zero. (5) Over the DVR/PID, the 2-term finite-free resolution plus perfect-cohomology assembly gives P; I checked the torsion O_E/varpi^a case. (6) On the single stratum, the bounded flat complex is K-flat, which is condition (ii) of the characterization; the unit on projective summands is natural. (7) Triangle identity, cone closure, the sections/reduction comparison at N=K, step 4 and the completeness triangle give K=0. This also holds under the blueprint_update wording of def-weil-derived-complete. (8) Naturality is genuinely elementary. All hypotheses hold where used: Lambda finite; s noetherian, of dimension 0, with ell invertible; boundedness for K-flatness.
